gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Xbox Wireless support is built into the headset itself and not into its USB dongle. SteelSeries says the Arctis Nova 5 and Nova 5P won't work with Xbox even if you buy the Nova 5X dongle separately. Microsoft says the only headsets Series X|S takes are officially licensed accessories over USB, or any headset plugged into the controller's 3.5 mm port.
standout_why: SoundGuys (cited) gives per-product results such as 'lack of Xbox support' for the Alienware Pro and an 'official Xbox license' for the CloudX Flight 2, but never explains why. The GamesRadar page (cited) returned no body text. The RTINGS gaming list says nothing about how Xbox connects. GamingReviewGuide (rank 4, not cited) already states the rule: 'Xbox Series X|S: does not accept generic USB audio dongles' and '3.5 mm wired: the universal fallback.' So rivals have part of it. What none of them has: Microsoft's own wording, and SteelSeries saying a 5X dongle can't make a Nova 5 or 5P work on Xbox, so the X or non-X choice is fixed at purchase.
decides: For 'PC or console', the plan works on every platform in only two ways. One is a headset whose own hardware is the Xbox variant, such as the Arctis Nova 5X with its dongle switched between 'Xbox' and 'USB'. The other is a wired 3.5 mm 4-pole CTIA plug into the controller, as on the HyperX Cloud III. This backs ChatGPT's Nova 5X and Cloud III picks. It also warns against the cheaper Nova 5 and 5P, which can't be fixed later by buying a dongle. The G Pro X 2's LIGHTSPEED wireless is not an Xbox option on Logitech's own page, which never mentions Xbox. A shopper who might add an Xbox should buy the X model or plan to stay wired.

findings.label: Which headsets Xbox Series X|S accepts, in Microsoft's words
findings.value: 'Any officially licensed Xbox One accessory that connects to your console wired or wirelessly via USB'; 'any headsets that connects via your Xbox Wireless Controller's 3.5mm port will also be supported'
findings.note: Microsoft's announcement of what carries over to Series X|S. USB only covers officially licensed accessories. The controller's 3.5 mm jack takes any headset.

findings.label: Optical-cable headsets on Series X|S
findings.value: 'Some gaming headsets that utilize an optical cable may require a firmware update to support game and chat audio over USB'; without updates, connect them 'directly to your televisions optical port'
findings.note: Matters for older base-station headsets that relied on Xbox One-era optical audio.

findings.label: Xbox support is in the headset, not the dongle
findings.value: 'The Arctis Nova 5X is the only Nova 5 model built for Xbox.' 'The Nova 5 and Nova 5P won't work with Xbox—even if you'd purchase the Nova 5X dongle separately.'
findings.source_title: Nova 5 Connection Issues Troubleshooting – SteelSeries Support

findings.label: Dongle mode switch
findings.value: Two positions: 'Xbox for Xbox Series X|S or Xbox One' and 'USB for PC, PlayStation, or other platforms'
findings.source_title: Nova 5 Connection Issues Troubleshooting – SteelSeries Support
findings.note: The same 5X dongle covers both console families, but the switch must be set for the system it is plugged into.

findings.label: Connectors and compatibility
findings.value: Wired 3.5 mm (4-pole CTIA) and wired USB (USB-C with a USB-A adapter). Compatible with PC, PS5, PS4, Xbox Series X|S, Xbox One, Nintendo Switch and mobile.
findings.source_title: HyperX Announces Cloud III Gaming Headset – HyperX press release
findings.note: A 4-pole CTIA plug carries both mic and audio through the controller jack, the route Microsoft supports for any headset. HyperX does not say which connector Xbox uses.
